content.text: I would like the CLI commands to be automatically generated from the API. When a change is made in the API, or GData, diagnostics, and such, the changes should be automatically carried over into the CLI. This ensures that the definitions are in one place, there is one ground truth definition, the docstrings are in one place, and changes are consistent. The same verbage is used in both script mode and the CLI. An argument to a function has the same CLI argument with --. Plan this refactor to enforce consistency in a CLI_GENERATOR.md
I’ll map the current public API, Click command registration, and import-contract tests, then write a staged refactor plan that makes API signatures and docstrings the sole CLI source of truth.

The current CLI is already thin at execution time, but it still duplicates command names, option declarations, defaults, help text, and diagnostic dispatch tables across dozens of modules. I’m now separating what can be derived mechanically from API metadata from the genuinely CLI-only pipeline policies.

The plan will use runtime generation, not checked-in generated Python. API signatures, annotations, defaults, and docstrings will compile directly into Click commands; only pipeline routing and legacy compatibility remain CLI-owned. It will also make unsupported or undocumented API parameters fail generation instead of silently becoming strings.

input.input:
const patch = "*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /home/maxwell-rosen/postgkyl/CLI_GENERATOR.md
+# API-driven CLI generator
+
+Status: implementation plan. This document does not change the CLI yet.
+
+## Outcome
+
+Every scientific `pgkyl` command will be compiled at runtime from the public
+Python callable that implements the same operation. The callable is the sole
+source of its name, parameters, types, requiredness, defaults, choices, and
+documentation. Adding or changing an exposed API parameter therefore changes
+the CLI automatically; an unsupported or undocumented parameter makes command
+generation fail with a precise error.
+
+There will be no generated Python files to commit and no per-command Click
+shells to keep synchronized.
+
+The canonical correspondence is reversible:
+
+```text
+Python                                      CLI
+data.interpolate(num_interp=4)              interpolate --num-interp 4
+data.fit(fit_type="exp2", window=True)       fit --fit-type exp2 --window
+five_moment.pressure(data, gas_gamma=1.4)   five-moment-pressure --gas-gamma 1.4
+```
+
+`snake_case` becomes `kebab-case`; no other canonical renaming is allowed.
+The dataset receiver is supplied by the chained working set. Every other
+parameter of an exposed callable is a `--long-option`, including parameters
+that are positional in Python. The existing bare-filename syntax remains a
+front-end shorthand for `load --file-name ...`.
+
+## Why the current structure can drift
+
+The current CLI has 52 hand-written `@click.command` shells under
+`src/postgkyl/cli/commands/`, 479 direct `@click.option` declarations, and 109
+uses of shared option decorators. Those shells repeat facts already present in
+the API:
+
+- `GData.interpolate` declares `num_interp`, `tag`, and `label`, while
+  `cli/commands/interpolate.py` redeclares their names, types, defaults, and
+  help.
+- `GData.select` and `cli/commands/select.py` separately list `comp` and
+  `z0` through `z5`.
+- `five_moment.VARIABLES`, `ten_moment.VARIABLES`, and `mhd.VARIABLES` are the
+  API vocabularies, but three CLI shells separately select options and filter
+  function arguments.
+- `render.matplotlib.plot` has the real plotting signature and documentation,
+  while `cli/commands/plot.py` owns another large option surface and semantic
+  preprocessing layer.
+- Several CLI names differ from their API names (`dg_local_poly`,
+  `evalatcoordproj`, `extractinput`, `mapping_file`, `nodes`, `block`, and
+  `c2p_vel`), so a caller must learn two vocabularies.
+- Some shells already use `inspect.signature` to recover API defaults
+  (`gk_rz` and `gk_fluxsurf`). This fixes only one duplicated fact and leaves
+  names, types, help, and accepted parameters duplicated.
+
+The refactor must remove the second declarations, not add broader parity tests
+around them.
+
+## Scope
+
+The generated surface includes:
+
+- public `GData` verbs and their functional operation equivalents;
+- public multi-dataset functions from `postgkyl.gdata.verbs`;
+- public render and I/O operations intended for command-line use;
+- public diagnostic functions, including equation-specific diagnostics,
+  gyrokinetic loaders, and program-scale diagnostics; and
+- public convenience compositions that currently exist only as CLI code.
+
+The following are front-end mechanics rather than scientific API operations
+and remain hand-written in `cli/`:
+
+- the chained Click group, `--version`, abbreviation, and bare-file dispatch;
+- working-set activation and `status`;
+- global session policy such as batch mode and output prefix; and
+- generic result presentation and legacy syntax warnings.
+
+`print` may remain a working-set inspector. `listoutputs`, `growth`, style
+mutation, frame grouping, and any other command that performs domain work must
+either gain a public API callable and be generated from it or be removed. An
+explicit test-owned allowlist will be limited to the true front-end commands;
+adding to it requires an architectural justification.
+
+Not every Python callable must be exposed. Callables that inherently require a
+Python object, such as `apply(fn)`, may be marked non-CLI with a reason. The
+public-surface audit described below ensures that exclusion is explicit rather
+than accidental.
+
+## Source-of-truth model
+
+Each fact has one owner:
+
+| Fact | Authoritative home |
+| --- | --- |
+| Command and option names | Python callable and parameter names |
+| Description and option help | The callable's docstring |
+| Type, optionality, and repeated shape | Type annotations |
+| Requiredness and default | The Python signature |
+| Choice vocabulary | `Enum`, `Literal`, or an API registry/provider |
+| CLI exposure, section, and pipeline behavior | Frozen metadata attached to the callable |
+| Working-set state and `--use` | Generic CLI runtime |
+| Deprecated spellings | One temporary `cli/compat.py` table |
+
+Click decorators are machinery and live only in the generator. API modules do
+not import Click.
+
+### Pure metadata leaf
+
+Add `src/postgkyl/command_spec/`, a dependency-free leaf containing frozen data
+records and decorators that attach those records to callables. It must not
+import `click`, `GData`, operations, diagnostics, renderers, or I/O.
+
+The exact records should be small and closed:
+
+```python
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class CommandSpec:
+  section: Section
+  execution: Execution
+  consumes_inputs: bool = False
+  selectable: bool = True
+  result: ResultPolicy = ResultPolicy.DATA
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class DatasetRef:
+  """Resolve this API dataset parameter from a working-set tag."""
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class CliHidden:
+  reason: str
+```
+
+`Section`, `Execution`, and `ResultPolicy` are enums, not strings. Constructors
+validate combinations so, for example, a loader cannot also request a mapped
+working-set receiver. The decorator returns the original callable and stores
+one immutable spec on it; it does not register global state.
+
+Use `typing.Annotated` only when a type alone cannot express lossless CLI
+lowering. Expected markers include `DatasetRef`, a dynamic choice provider,
+and a key/value mapping codec. They may refine parsing but may not override a
+parameter name, default, or help text.
+
+### Deterministic discovery
+
+Do not maintain another `COMMANDS` list. `cli/discovery.py` walks these public
+roots deterministically:
+
+1. `GData.__dict__` and the explicitly typed, non-broadcast methods of
+   `GDataGroup`;
+2. facade exports in `postgkyl.__all__`;
+3. modules exported by `postgkyl.diagnostics.__all__`, recursively for public
+   diagnostic subpackages; and
+4. public registry values such as the moment `VARIABLES` tables.
+
+Only objects carrying `CommandSpec` are emitted. Public candidate callables
+must carry either `CommandSpec` or `CliHidden`; an unclassified callable is a
+CI error. Discovery rejects two callables that lower to the same command name
+unless they are mechanically linked functional/fluent views of the same
+canonical callable.
+
+There is no import-order registry and no filesystem/module-name scan. A new
+public diagnostic module becomes discoverable by adding it to the owning
+package's `__all__`, which is already the authoritative public-export fact.
+
+### One callable behind functional, fluent, and CLI forms
+
+Core operations currently repeat signatures and abbreviated docstrings in
+`GData`. Introduce an earned `fluent` binding for the many exact delegations:
+
+```python
+interpolate = fluent(operations.interpolate)
+```
+
+The binding drops the operation's leading dataset parameter from the bound
+method signature, forwards all remaining arguments unchanged, and preserves
+the canonical signature, docstring, annotations, and `CommandSpec` for
+introspection. It adds no defaults or conversions. Exceptional methods whose
+return type needs fluent wrapping, such as `val2coord`, may stay explicit and
+be their own canonical callable.
+
+Render forwarding layers must likewise preserve the renderer's signature and
+docstring mechanically. Public command sources may not expose an opaque
+`**kwargs`; forwarded parameters must remain inspectable. This makes a change
+to the canonical operation visible simultaneously in the functional API, the
+fluent API, and the generated CLI.
+
+## Signature-to-Click contract
+
+`cli/compiler.py` performs a strict, total lowering from an inspected callable
+to an immutable intermediate `CommandModel`, then from that model to
+`click.Command`. Keeping inspection separate from Click construction makes the
+contract testable without parsing argv.
+
+| Python form | Canonical CLI form |
+| --- | --- |
+| `some_name` | `--some-name` |
+| required parameter | required option |
+| `T | None = None` | optional option, default `None` |
+| `bool = False/True` | `--flag/--no-flag`, with the signature's default |
+| `str`, `int`, `float`, `Path` | matching Click scalar type |
+| `Enum` or `Literal[...]` | `click.Choice` using those exact values |
+| `list[T]` or variadic tuple | repeatable option |
+| fixed tuple | one option with fixed `nargs` |
+| mapping record | repeatable `--name key=value` through one generic codec |
+| annotated dataset parameter | `--parameter TAG`, resolved from the working set |
+| bound `self` or annotated pipeline receiver | injected from the working set; no option |
+
+Additional rules:
+
+- All user-supplied parameters are options. The generator emits no
+  `click.argument`, eliminating chained-command ordering surprises for `fit`,
+  `evaluate`, `integrate`, and `map`.
+- Requiredness comes only from absence of a Python default. `Optional[T]`
+  permits `None`; it does not by itself make a parameter optional.
+- Defaults are never reconstructed, evaluated from help text, or copied into
+  CLI modules.
+- The compiler uses `typing.get_type_hints(..., include_extras=True)` and
+  rejects unresolved forward references.
+- An unannotated parameter, `Any`, unsupported union, arbitrary callable,
+  `*args`, or `**kwargs` is a generation error unless the whole callable is
+  explicitly `CliHidden`.
+- No fallback silently treats an unknown type as `str`.
+- Short flags are not generated. Existing short flags may exist only as
+  deprecated aliases in the compatibility layer.
+- Click receives the parameter name unchanged internally. Only the reversible
+  underscore-to-hyphen presentation transform is applied.
+
+This contract requires normalizing some APIs before exposure. For example,
+`pg.load(..., **read_kwargs)` must replace the open-ended kwargs with explicit
+common parameters and/or a typed `read_options` mapping. Public plot entry
+points must separate representable plot options from private `Figure` and
+callback machinery. A narrower, honest callable is preferable to a generator
+exception.
+
+## Docstring contract
+
+The canonical callable owns one Google-style docstring:
+
+- its first paragraph is the command's short and long description;
+- every exposed parameter has exactly one entry under `Args:`;
+- parameter descriptions do not restate defaults, because Click displays the
+  signature default;
+- `Returns:` and `Raises:` remain API documentation and may be appended to
+  long help, but never define invocation behavior; and
+- fluent bindings inherit the canonical docstring instead of adding “see
+  operations...” copies.
+
+Implement one small, strict parser for the subset above. Generation fails when
+an exposed parameter is undocumented, a documented name is absent from the
+signature, or a docstring is missing. The error names the fully qualified
+callable and parameter. Do not place help strings in `CommandSpec` or
+`click.option` calls.
+
+Dynamic text such as the available evaluate operators or gyrokinetic
+quantities is derived from the same public registry/provider used for API
+validation and shell completion. It is not interpolated from a CLI-side copy.
+
+## Chained execution is generic CLI machinery
+
+Signatures describe invocation; `CommandSpec.execution` describes how a pure
+API call participates in the CLI working set. The runtime has a closed set of
+adapters:
+
+| Execution | Input binding | Working-set effect |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| `MAP_REPLACE` | each selected active dataset | replace that dataset with the returned dataset |
+| `MAP_APPEND` | each selected active dataset | keep inputs and append results |
+| `COMBINE` | active datasets or named `DatasetRef`s | call once, optionally consume inputs, append result(s) |
+| `TERMINAL_EACH` | each selected active dataset | present values; do not change datasets |
+| `TERMINAL_ALL` | all selected active datasets | call once and present; do not change datasets |
+| `LOAD` | no working-set input | flatten and append returned dataset(s) |
+| `SESSION` | `DataSpace` only | reserved for the small manual front-end allowlist |
+
+The adapter binds arguments by signature and calls the API with no
+command-specific branches. It catches the documented user-input exceptions
+(`ValueError`, `TypeError`, and file errors) at the edge and reports a
+`click.UsageError`; unexpected exceptions retain their traceback in testing.
+
+`--use` is added mechanically when `selectable=True`. It belongs to the
+working-set runtime, not to every API signature. `tag`, `label`, `inplace`,
+and all scientific controls are generated from the callable when present.
+Named dataset inputs use their API parameter names (`--density`, `--momentum`,
+`--bfield`) and resolve a tag to exactly one active dataset, with missing and
+duplicate matches reported explicitly.
+
+Result presentation is separate from computation. Generic presenters cover
+datasets, dataset sequences, strings, paths, scalars/arrays, and figures.
+Special reports should become typed API return records with a presenter for
+that record type, rather than custom command callbacks that reach into a
+dataset's `ctx`.
+
+## Diagnostic naming
+
+Generate one command per public diagnostic function. Prefix it with its public
+module path to avoid collisions while retaining the Python vocabulary:
+
+```text
+five_moment.pressure     -> five-moment-pressure
+ten_moment.pressure      -> ten-moment-pressure
+mhd.pressure             -> mhd-pressure
+multispecies.energetics  -> multispecies-energetics
+gyrokinetics.gk_rz       -> gyrokinetics-gk-rz
+```
+
+The moment `VARIABLES` mappings remain the one home for quantity aliases used
+by programmatic lookup, but the canonical CLI no longer constructs a union
+signature behind `euler --variable-name`, `tenmoment --variable-name`, or
+`mhd --variable-name`. Direct commands give each function its exact options
+and exact docstring. The three dispatcher commands remain temporary legacy
+adapters and lower to the direct generated commands.
+
+Do not strip or invent diagnostic parameter names. For example, the canonical
+agyrotropy flags come from `ten_moment.agyro(ptensor, bfield, measure=...)` and
+are therefore `--ptensor`, `--bfield`, and `--measure`; `--pressure` is only a
+legacy alias.
+
+## Move existing CLI semantics to their rightful owner
+
+Before deleting a shell, classify each behavior in it:
+
+| Current area | Canonical owner after refactor |
+| --- | --- |
+| `interpolate`, `select`, `fft`, `magsq`, `mask`, `differentiate`, `average`, `eval_at_coord_proj`, `map` | operation signature/docstring plus generic `MAP_REPLACE` |
+| `collect`, `sort`, `evaluate`, `relchange`, animations | multi-dataset API signature plus `COMBINE`/`TERMINAL_ALL` |
+| `fit` report and `growth` preset | public fit/growth result types and API functions; CLI only presents them |
+| moment and multi-input diagnostics | each public diagnostic function plus `DatasetRef` binding |
+| gyrokinetic loaders/programs and PKPM | existing public loader/program callable after signature normalization |
+| plot/Plotly/PyVista behavior | public render operation; overlay/range/default decisions leave the CLI shell |
+| load basis codes and frame/species parsing | public value/parser types shared by script and CLI callers |
+| balance boundary-file packing | typed API mapping/record, passed through one `--bflux-files` option |
+| batch/show/saveframe policy | CLI session adapter, applied uniformly to render commands |
+| activation, abbreviation, bare filename | CLI front end only |
+
+Important normalizations include:
+
+- `local_poly` becomes `local-poly`; `dg_local_poly` is legacy.
+- `eval_at_coord_proj` becomes `eval-at-coord-proj`; `evalatcoordproj` is
+  legacy.
+- `extract_input` becomes `extract-input`.
+- `map(mapping=...)` produces `--mapping`, not the CLI-only
+  `mapping_file`/`--mapping-file` spelling.
+- `load_gk_distf(use_c2p_vel=..., block_idx=...)` produces
+  `--use-c2p-vel` and `--block-idx`; shorter current names are legacy.
+- `save(out_name=..., extension=...)` produces `--out-name` and
+  `--extension`, not `--out` and `--format`.
+- Program APIs that take a `bflux_files` mapping receive that same CLI option;
+  the CLI must not privately explode it into six differently named flags.
+
+If current CLI preprocessing is useful to script callers, promote it to a
+public, typed function. If it is only presentation, keep it in a generic
+presenter. Do not hide it in generator conditionals keyed by command name.
+
+## Generated registration
+
+Replace `cli/commands/__init__.py`'s imports, `COMMANDS`, and
+`COMMAND_SECTIONS` with derived values:
+
+```python
+models = compile_public_surface(postgkyl)
+commands = tuple(build_click_command(model) for model in models)
+sections = group_by_section(models)
+```
+
+Ordering is deterministic: section enum order, explicit spec order only where
+workflow order matters, then canonical command name. `PgkylGroup` continues to
+render flat sectioned help and unique-prefix abbreviation over the generated
+commands.
+
+The build validates the entire surface before registering any command. One bad
+spec must not produce a partially populated CLI.
+
+## Compatibility policy
+
+Land the generated canonical syntax without immediately removing working 2.x
+scripts:
+
+1. `cli/compat.py` contains frozen declarative aliases from old command/option
+   spellings and the four old positional arguments to canonical generated
+   options.
+2. A legacy invocation prints one deprecation warning and invokes the same
+   generated command model; it does not call a separate scientific callback.
+3. Current integration tests run once against canonical syntax and, for the
+   compatibility window, a focused set runs against legacy syntax.
+4. New commands and options may not add legacy aliases.
+5. Remove the table and legacy tests at the next declared major release.
+
+Unique-prefix abbreviation remains a presentation convenience and is not an
+alias declaration. Existing hidden aliases such as `pl` and `ev` move into the
+same compatibility table.
+
+## Layering changes
+
+The new dependency direction is:
+
+```text
+command_spec (frozen records; no internal imports)
+       ^              ^                 ^
+       |              |                 |
+operations/gdata   diagnostics       public render/I/O owners
+       \              |                 /
+        \             |                /
+             facade/public exports
+                      |
+                      v
+        cli discovery -> compiler -> runtime -> Click
+```
+
+Update `tests/test_postgkyl.py::_ALLOWED` first, then update the matching
+AGENTS.md diagrams in the same commit. At minimum, add the `command_spec` leaf
+and only the edges actually used by owners of command metadata; allow `cli` to
+read the facade and `command_spec`. `command_spec` itself has an empty allowed
+import set. The CLI still does not import implementation modules to find
+defaults or vocabularies.
+
+## Migration sequence
+
+### 1. Characterize the current surface
+
+- Build a test-only manifest of current command names, long options, types,
+  defaults, requiredness, and section.
+- Classify all 52 commands into generated API operations, promoted API
+  compositions, and the minimal front-end allowlist.
+- Record intentional canonical renames and legacy translations.
+- Keep the existing end-to-end CLI tests as behavior characterization.
+
+Exit condition: every current command has one named canonical API owner or a
+documented removal/front-end exception.
+
+### 2. Add the schema and strict compiler
+
+- Implement frozen metadata records, validated decorators, and type codecs in
+  `command_spec/`.
+- Implement docstring parsing and callable-to-`CommandModel` compilation with
+  no Click dependency.
+- Implement `CommandModel`-to-Click lowering and generic execution adapters in
+  `cli/`.
+- Add dummy-callable unit tests covering every supported and rejected
+  signature form.
+
+Exit condition: an isolated annotated function can generate correct help,
+parse argv, and call the function with exactly the expected Python values.
+
+### 3. Normalize the public API
+
+- Give every candidate an explicit complete signature, resolved annotations,
+  and one complete Google-style docstring.
+- Replace CLI-facing `**kwargs` with typed parameters or typed option records.
+- Add `fluent()` bindings for exact `GData` delegations and preserve signatures
+  through render/operation forwarding.
+- Add public API functions/result records for useful CLI-only compositions
+  such as `growth`; explicitly hide genuinely Python-only callables.
+- Make public `__all__` lists accurately describe discovery roots.
+
+Exit condition: the public-surface classification test passes without
+generating Click commands.
+
+### 4. Migrate core verbs and loaders
+
+- Annotate load, transform, combine, terminal, I/O, and render callables with
+  `CommandSpec`.
+- Register generated commands beside the old shells under temporary test-only
+  names and compare their parsed calls and working-set effects.
+- Move semantic preprocessing out of `plot`, `animate`, `load`, `fit`, and
+  `integrate` shells.
+- Switch canonical registration to generated commands once parity or an
+  intentional behavior change is covered.
+
+Exit condition: no core scientific command has a hand-written Click callback.
+
+### 5. Migrate diagnostics
+
+- Classify and annotate public moment, rotation, multispecies, kinetic, PKPM,
+  and gyrokinetic functions.
+- Generate one namespaced command per diagnostic function.
+- Replace tag-renaming shells with generic `DatasetRef` binding.
+- Replace `euler`/`tenmoment`/`mhd` and program shells with declarative legacy
+  adapters to generated commands.
+
+Exit condition: adding a documented parameter to any exposed diagnostic makes
+the corresponding generated help and invocation accept it without a CLI edit.
+
+### 6. Delete duplicated declarations
+
+- Delete migrated modules under `cli/commands/`, `_options.py`, `_variable.py`,
+  and command-specific argument conversion helpers.
+- Derive registration and help sections from discovered models.
+- Retain only app/group code, working-set runtime, generic codecs/presenters,
+  and the bounded compatibility table.
+- Update README examples and `examples/cli_tutorial.md` to canonical long
+  options and names.
+
+Exit condition: `rg '@click\.(command|option|argument)' src/postgkyl/cli`
+finds decorators only in the group/front-end and generator machinery, never a
+scientific command definition.
+
+### 7. Remove compatibility at the major-version boundary
+
+- Remove legacy aliases, positional translations, and dispatcher commands.
+- Delete legacy-only tests and documentation.
+- Keep the canonical schema/property/end-to-end tests permanently.
+
+## Enforcement tests
+
+Add focused tests with the following properties:
+
+1. **Public classification:** every public candidate is exactly one of exposed
+   or hidden-with-reason.
+2. **Total compilation:** all exposed callables compile; no unknown annotation,
+   unresolved forward reference, missing doc, `*args`, or `**kwargs` passes.
+3. **Exact projection:** excluding injected receivers, the set of generated
+   long options is exactly the callable parameter set after `_` to `-`.
+4. **Signature parity:** option type, requiredness, multiplicity, and default
+   equal the inspected annotation and signature.
+5. **Help provenance:** command and option help equal parsed canonical
+   docstring sections.
+6. **Round trip:** representative argv for every codec binds to the same value
+   used in a direct Python call.
+7. **Invocation equivalence:** a generated command invokes its canonical
+   callable once with the exact bound arguments and no undeclared conversion.
+8. **Working-set laws:** each execution enum has property tests for active,
+   inactive, selected, consumed, replaced, and appended datasets.
+9. **Inventory integrity:** command names are unique, sections are complete,
+   ordering is deterministic, and the manual command allowlist is exact.
+10. **No duplicated Click surface:** an AST test rejects scientific
+    `@click.command`, `@click.option`, and `@click.argument` declarations
+    outside the generator/front-end allowlist.
+11. **Architecture:** the existing import-contract and acyclic-graph tests
+    include `command_spec`.
+12. **End to end:** representative load-transform-diagnostic-render chains run
+    through `CliRunner`, alongside the existing numerical/API tests.
+
+Do not use a hand-maintained golden option manifest as the permanent parity
+test; it would become another source of truth. The phase-1 manifest is only a
+migration aid and is deleted when the old shells are deleted.
+
+## Definition of done
+
+The refactor is complete when:
+
+- changing an exposed callable's parameter name, annotation, default, choice
+  vocabulary, or docstring changes `pgkyl <command> --help` with no CLI edit;
+- adding a public exposed callable produces a command after only API-local
+  metadata is supplied;
+- unsupported public signatures fail CI with a local, actionable error;
+- functional, fluent, and CLI calls reach the same canonical function with the
+  same parameter values;
+- no scientific command owns a Click callback or option declaration;
+- CLI-only state and compatibility facts remain isolated and bounded; and
+- all import-contract, schema, working-set, numerical, and end-to-end tests
+  pass.
*** End Patch";
text(await tools.apply_patch(patch));

content.text:
Created [CLI_GENERATOR.md](/home/maxwell-rosen/postgkyl/CLI_GENERATOR.md) with the runtime-generation architecture, migration phases, compatibility strategy, and enforcement tests.

Only documentation was changed; `git diff --check` passes.
